candidates.change_summary: Remove the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so pastBlockTime never updates after a successful call.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so a different value is stored.
Change `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime);` to `require(block.timestamp >= pastBlockTime);` allowing a second call in the same block that then updates pastBlockTime.
Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the state variable pastBlockTime is never updated.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the stored value differs after each call.
Replace the assignment with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so the stored value is one more than the timestamp.
Remove the statement that transfers the contract balance back to the caller, so the contract retains the funds when block.number % 15 == 0.
Change the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 == 1 so payouts occur on different blocks.
Change the value requirement from msg.value == 10 ether to msg.value >= 10 ether, allowing calls with more than 10 ether to succeed and altering the contract balance and accepted call sequences.
Remove the statement pastBlockTime = block.timestamp; so the time-guard state is never updated and the observable state via public getter differs.
Replace the time guard condition block.timestamp > pastBlockTime with block.timestamp >= pastBlockTime, allowing multiple calls in the same block and changing which calls succeed.
Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so pastBlockTime remains 0, which is observable via its public getter.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the state variable stores a different value observable via its public getter.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so the stored value differs by one, observable via its public getter.
Move `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` after the if-block; if the transfer throws (transfer can revert on failure), the update is skipped and pastBlockTime differs.
